clue.text: Shy, lean, semi-retired officers

parts.note: a shy person is reserved, keeping to themselves
a ship that leans to one side is said to list

explanation.surface: Officers in semi-retirement described as timid and thin.
explanation.definitionFit: The reserved list is the roster of retired military officers who remain liable to be recalled, so its members are only half retired.

clue.text: Insist that the lost sheep has returned to the fold

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, here the stray one
a sheep back in its fold is home

explanation.surface: A parable-like picture of a stray animal finally safe in its pen.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive a point home forcefully is to insist on it until it is accepted.

clue.text: Wade and see form of marine flora

indicators.note: a new form of the letters means they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Paddling in the shallows to look at plants of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges WADE and SEE together; 'and' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kelp and wrack are plants of the ocean, the commonest kind of marine vegetation.

clue.text: So fat, beer is served with it for dinner

indicators.note: food served up is dished out in a new arrangement, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A fatty joint is accompanied by beer at the evening meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is served' rearranges SO FAT and BEER; 'with it for' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional English Sunday roast of beef is a classic main meal.

clue.text: Finish with one's tail in the air

definitions.text: with one's tail in the air

explanation.surface: An animal finishing with its rear pointed skyward.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish somewhere; read literally, the end (tail) is up (raised).

clue.text: Nothing's right when a boor's about, so watch it!

indicators.note: the boor stands about, i.e. around, the other letters

parts.note: a lout is a boorish, uncouth person
nothing is zero, the letter O
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A warning that when a rude oaf is around, nothing is right.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are warnings to be careful and stay alert.

clue.text: A pig of a question!

parts.note: a pig makes snorting noises, and a very tough question is informally one that makes you snort

explanation.surface: Exasperation at a really difficult question.
explanation.definitionFit: A snorter is informal British slang for something remarkable, especially a very difficult problem; a pig literally snorts.

clue.text: Tommy intends to get unearned income

parts.note: Tommy Atkins is the nickname for a British private soldier
to intend something is to mean it

explanation.surface: A soldier plans to come by money without working.
explanation.walkthrough: Tommy is the old British nickname for an ordinary soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Private means are personal wealth such as investments, money one has without working for it.

clue.text: To dance with graduate is sweet

parts.note: the rumba is a Cuban dance
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: Dancing with a graduate is a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A rum baba is a small rum-soaked sponge cake served as a dessert.

clue.text: Decline to have forty winks

explanation.surface: Refusing a quick nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop-off is a fall in amount; to drop off is to fall asleep briefly.

clue.text: Sack the team before a lecture or heart to heart chat

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
a team is a side in sport
a lecture is a talk

explanation.surface: A manager dismisses the squad before a dressing-down, or a cosy chat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fireside talk is an intimate, informal conversation, as if held by the hearth.

clue.text: Turbulent oil caught in the escape valve

annotationWithheld.why: Turbulent oil caught in the escape valve (7): VENT around an anagram of OIL needs 'Turbulent' as both the definition and the anagram indicator
annotationWithheld.clue: Turbulent oil caught in the escape valve

clue.text: Disciplinarian in favour of a hundred to run

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone backing a hundred runs, like a cricket fan.
explanation.definitionFit: A proctor is a university officer responsible for keeping students in order.

clue.text: Walk on the sole of a shoe

explanation.surface: Stepping on the underside of footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To tread is to step or walk on something; the tread is the patterned underside of a sole.

clue.text: Generous credit given for simple language

explanation.surface: Lenient lending explained in plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are lenient repayment arrangements; read literally, the words mean uncomplicated expressions.

clue.text: Pay debt before the evil becomes well established

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay what is owed
sin is wrongdoing, evil

explanation.surface: Clear what you owe before wickedness takes root.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who settles in becomes comfortable and at home in a new place.

clue.text: Type of jade Jack Sprat was allergic to?

explanation.surface: A gemstone the nursery-rhyme character couldn't stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Jack Sprat could eat no fat.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton-fat jade is a creamy white nephrite; meat fat is literally what Sprat avoided.

clue.text: Autumn which led to Adam and eve's winter

definitions.text: which led to Adam and eve's winter

explanation.surface: The season that brought Eden's paradise to a cold end.
explanation.definitionFit: Fall is the American word for autumn; the Fall is mankind's expulsion from Eden.

clue.text: A final comment which is unhyphenated

explanation.surface: Closing remarks about a compound written solid.
explanation.definitionFit: 'In a word' sums things up briefly; a compound written as a single unbroken word needs no hyphen.

clue.text: Dad having married repeatedly put his foot down

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A father with several weddings behind him finally got firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that paws strikes the ground over and over with its feet.

clue.text: Cue given to Bertie if there is a "plant" on the table

parts.note: the instruction given to a snooker player with a cue is to pot the ball
Herb is a short form of Herbert, as Bertie is

explanation.surface: A snooker player prompted to sink a planted ball.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker a plant is a set-up shot; the culinary sense is a herb eaten at the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot herb is a leafy plant grown for cooking, so it ends up on the dining table.

clue.text: Donning habit can be exhausting

explanation.surface: Putting on a nun's habit can be tiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Donning clothes is putting them on; a tiring task is wearing.

clue.text: Eternal exhortation of the keep-young lobby

explanation.surface: An undying slogan from anti-ageing campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: Timeless things never grow old; read as two words it urges people to grow old less.

clue.text: Depressed at Camp David's failure he would have been

definitions.text: Camp David's failure he would have been

parts.note: depressed means sad

explanation.surface: A leader downcast at the collapse of peace talks.
explanation.walkthrough: Camp David was the 1978 Egypt-Israel peace summit; the Egyptian president there was the man in question.
explanation.definitionFit: Anwar Sadat, Egypt's president, signed the Camp David accords and would have shared any blame for a collapse.

clue.text: Give way lest Pat becomes troubled

indicators.note: letters that become troubled are disturbed into a new order

explanation.surface: Yield in case Pat gets upset.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone past is to yield and allow them through.

clue.text: Admiral gets official stamp if not deceased

parts.note: a seal is a stamp of authority on a document
or means otherwise, if not
D is the abbreviation for died, deceased

explanation.surface: A naval chief receives an official stamp, provided he is still alive.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sea Lord is a senior admiral on the British naval board.

clue.text: Particular place is reserved

indicators.note: read as re-served, the letters are served up again in another order

explanation.surface: A fussy diner insists their seat is booked.
explanation.definitionFit: Special and particular both mean distinctive or specific to one case.

clue.text: Case brought by Victorian PM against an old crone

parts.note: William Gladstone was a British prime minister under Queen Victoria
bag is a derogatory word for an unpleasant old woman

explanation.surface: Luggage carried by a nineteenth-century premier opposing a hag.
explanation.definitionFit: A Gladstone bag is a hinged leather travelling case named after the statesman.
